newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-COLOGNE FACE TRANSFER REQUEST FROM STRIKER POLSTER. [CORRECTED 14:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-COLOGNE FACE TRANSFER REQUEST FROM STRIKER POLSTER. [CORRECTED 14:25 GMT]

text.p: Bundesliga pace-setters Cologne, who lost both their goalkeeper and a German Cup tie last week, now face a transfer request from striker Toni Polster.

Cologne have languished in the lower part of the table for the past four seasons but were leaders after winning their first three matches (corrects to make clear Cologne are not currently leading the table).
The club's fortunes began to unravel with a home league defeat to Rostock. Former international goalkeeper Bodo Illgner left for Real Madrid and they also lost to second division Zwickau in the Cup.
Now they must travel to second-placed VfB Stuttgart with Austrian international Polster saying he wants to leave because of disagreements with trainer Peter Neururer.
"We are not on the same wave length anymore and it would be best if we were to make a clean break right now -- better yesterday than today," Polster said.

"It is not because I am sitting on the bench," added Polster, who came on to score two goals in the last four minutes in Cologne's 3-1 win over Freiburg three weeks ago. "Too much has gone wrong between Neururer and me."
Neururer saved Cologne from relegation last season but has alienated the 32-year-old Austrian, scorer of 47 goals for Cologne in 87 Bundesliga matches.
The coach showed no sign he would promote Polster from the role of super-sub. "There will be no changes in the starting line-up," he said.
VfB Stuttgart are the team of the moment, spearheaded by the multi-national striking trio of Bulgarian Krasimir Balakov, German Fredi Bobic and Brazilian Giovane Elber.
They have a 100 percent record after three games in which they have scored 10 goals, and trail leaders Bayern Munich, who has played four matches, by just one point.
In the weekend's other top ties, Bayern entertain promoted Bielefeld and champions Borussia Dortmund travel to ninth-placed Rostock.
